title: Designing the agentic layer of a clinical operations platform
blurb: Agentic SaaS interface that reduces complexity so a nurse has more time to focus on patient care.
copy: I joined a four-person pod tasked with designing the natural-language layer that would come next, starting from the hardest constraint in the room: the agent could never see the patient data it was reasoning about.

The work centered on a four-tier confidence model for reprocessing status, a small registry of purpose-built widgets instead of a single chat surface, and a PII boundary that had to hold on both the output and input side of every conversation. It shipped to a real private beta across three partner clinics in Germany and Spain.

title: Designing a natural language search tool for a clinical environment
blurb: At Olympus I led design on a traceability search tool that let clinical staff retrieve reprocessing records in seconds, with no SQL knowledge, no training, and no paper ledgers.
copy: I led design for a clinical traceability tool that helped hospital staff retrieve reprocessing records from complex structured data.
The work explored how to make high-stakes, low-frequency workflows feel understandable on first contact, using a guided query experience that reduced ambiguity and built confidence.

title: A music platform built around one constraint: one song per person per day
blurb: I designed and built Good Song Club independently — a platform where the only rule is one song per day, no algorithm. Two years in, it has crossed 10,000 posts and found a worldwide community.
copy: Good Song Club started from a personal frustration: there was no good place to share a single, considered music recommendation with friends. Streaming platforms optimise for volume; social media buries a link in noise.

The platform runs on two deliberate constraints — YouTube links only, one post per day — that define everything about how it feels to use it. I designed and built the entire product alone, from product strategy through front-end and back-end engineering.

title: Building a data-dense dashboard for autonomous vehicle sensors
blurb: At Cavnue I designed a dashboard that let engineers monitor the health of hundreds of roadside sensors across active AV corridors in real time.
copy: Cavnue is on a mission to bridge the gap between current autonomous vehicle capabilities and the promised future of full self-driving.
When I was brought on to the product team, our main goal was to take the overwhelming amount of data generated by Cavnue's hardware system and surface it in a way that was valuable to our end user.

title: Defining a passenger experience inside an all-electric rideshare fleet
blurb: At Revel I designed a bespoke tablet interface mounted in the back seat of every Tesla in the company's rideshare fleet, turning an untouched surface into an elevated passenger experience.
copy: I joined Revel as their first designer in the Summer of 2019 — a pivotal time in the company's growth. I was tasked with designing a full suite of internal tools that would allow the company to bring all their operations and logistics in-house.

I worked closely with nearly every department lead in the company to ensure that the tools we built met the needs of all who'd be using it. As a result, once we released the tools, we saw a huge spike in productivity and financial efficiency.

In addition to internal tools I was a key stakeholder on a number of user-facing, high-revenue initiatives. For example I led design for a unique, passenger facing tablet in the run-up to the launch of Revel's rideshare program in an effort to rise above the existing players in the market, flexing our position as a car-service provider that owned the end to end experience.
I also designed the sign-up, purchase funnel, and user dashboard experience for Revel's electric bike rental program.
